name: Pioglitazone

discovery.note: Part of Takeda's thiazolidinedione programme that began with ciglitazone.

tagline: An insulin sensitiser that switches on PPAR-gamma in fat, muscle and liver
summary: Pioglitazone is a thiazolidinedione that improves insulin sensitivity by activating the nuclear receptor PPAR-gamma. It lowers glucose durably with low hypoglycaemia risk and benefits fatty liver disease, but causes fluid retention and weight gain and is contraindicated in heart failure.
mechanism: Pioglitazone is a ligand for peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), a nuclear receptor expressed mainly in adipose tissue. Activation changes transcription of genes involved in glucose and lipid metabolism, promoting differentiation of small insulin-sensitive adipocytes, redistributing fat away from liver and muscle and increasing adiponectin.

The net effect is improved insulin sensitivity in muscle and liver and reduced hepatic glucose output. PPARγ activation in the kidney collecting duct increases sodium reabsorption, which explains oedema and heart-failure risk.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, monotherapy or combination
Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (guideline-supported, off-label in many regions)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Actos in July 1999, months after rosiglitazone.

history.title: Troglitazone withdrawn
history.detail: The first thiazolidinedione, troglitazone, is withdrawn for liver toxicity; pioglitazone shows no such signal.

history.title: PROactive trial
history.detail: PROactive reports a non-significant primary endpoint but fewer death, MI and stroke events in a secondary endpoint.

history.title: Heart failure boxed warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning on congestive heart failure to thiazolidinediones.

history.title: Bladder cancer concerns
history.detail: France and Germany suspend new prescriptions; FDA warns of a possible bladder cancer risk with use over one year.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic pioglitazone launches in the US in August 2012.

history.title: IRIS trial
history.detail: In insulin-resistant patients after stroke or TIA, pioglitazone reduces recurrent stroke or MI (NEJM 2016).

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP2C8 and CYP3A4 to active metabolites

safety.boxed_warning: Congestive heart failure: thiazolidinediones cause or exacerbate heart failure; not recommended in symptomatic heart failure and contraindicated in NYHA class III–IV.

facts: Pioglitazone was approved two months after rosiglitazone in 1999.
Its predecessor troglitazone was withdrawn in 2000 after cases of fatal liver failure.

references.title: Kernan WN et al. IRIS trial (NEJM 2016)
